Lip Blush in Jaipur | Lip Tint & Neutralization

Lip blush is a semi-permanent lip tint in which soft pigment is placed in the lips to even out their colour, define the lip line and give a natural flush. At Kezza, lip permanent makeup, including neutralization for darker lips, is done by our trained PMU artist at our Jaipur and Sikar clinics, after a patch test and a colour that you approve.

The Technique

What Is Lip Blush?

Lip blush uses a fine needle machine to place soft pigment into the upper layer of the lip skin. The colour is built up gently, often fading from a slightly stronger line to a softer centre, so the lips look naturally tinted rather than painted with lipstick. The shape can be subtly balanced where one side is uneven.

Straight after treatment the colour looks much brighter than the final result. As the lips heal, they flake and the colour can seem to disappear for a few days before it gradually returns softer and more even. The true healed colour shows after about four to six weeks, when a touch-up session perfects it. Lip blush usually lasts two to three years before a refresh is needed.

Lip neutralization is used for lips that are darker or have cool, bluish-brown tones. Warmer pigment is layered first to counteract the darkness, and a tint can then be added on top. Dark lips often need more than one session, can heal patchy or slightly ashy at first, and results vary with the starting colour and with habits such as smoking and sun exposure.

In Short:

  • Soft tint: natural colour rather than a lipstick look.
  • Bright at first: softens as the lips heal.
  • Lasts 2 to 3 years: with a refresh when it fades.

Suitability

Is Lip Blush Right for You?

Lip blush suits most healthy adults. A few conditions mean you should wait or take extra precautions.

Lip blush may suit you if

  • Your lips are pale, uneven in colour or have a faint border
  • Your lips are darker than you would like and you are interested in neutralization
  • You wear lipstick every day and want a soft colour that stays
  • You want lips to look fuller or more balanced without fillers

Wait, or check with us first, if

  • You get cold sores; a doctor may advise antiviral tablets before and after treatment
  • You have an active cold sore, cracked lips, a rash or an infection on or around the lips
  • You are pregnant or breastfeeding; we recommend waiting until afterwards
  • You have had lip fillers recently, form raised scars easily, or have reacted to tattoo pigment before

Lip PMU is often combined with brows. See our microblading and eyebrow PMU page.

Procedure

How a Lip Blush Appointment Works

Most of the first appointment is spent on the consultation, colour choice and numbing.

01

Consultation & Patch Test

At a consultation before your treatment day, the artist talks through the look you want, checks your lips and medical history, including cold sores, and does a patch test so any reaction has time to show.

02

Colour & Shape

Shades are tested against your skin, and the outline is drawn. Pigment is applied only after you approve both.

03

Numbing

A numbing cream is applied to the lips, and the area is cleaned with antiseptic.

04

Pigment in Layers

Colour is built up gradually with a fine needle, checking evenness and depth as the artist works.

05

Touch-Up at 4 to 6 Weeks

Once healed, a touch-up evens out the colour and fills any lighter spots.

Healing

Lip Blush Healing Timeline

Lips go through several colour changes before the final shade appears.

D1

Days 1 to 2

Lips look swollen and the colour looks bright and bold.

D4

Days 3 to 5

Lips feel dry and start to flake. Do not pick the flakes.

D10

Days 7 to 14

Colour can look faded or patchy for a while as the new skin settles.

W6

Weeks 4 to 6

The healed colour appears, and your touch-up session perfects it.

Y2

Two to Three Years

A colour refresh keeps the tint even as the pigment fades.

Medical Note: Results vary from person to person. This page is general information from Kezza Hair & Skin Clinic and is not a substitute for a consultation with a doctor.

Choosing your shade

The right colour depends on your skin undertone, your natural lip colour and the look you want. On many Indian skin tones, warm rose, peach and soft berry shades heal most naturally, while very cool pinks can look greyish on darker lips. The artist tests shades against your skin and explains how each is likely to heal, because the healed colour is always softer than the colour on the day. If your lips are dark, neutralization may be suggested before or with the tint, so the final shade looks clean rather than muddy.

Before your appointment

  • If you get cold sores, tell us when you book so a doctor can advise on antiviral tablets.
  • Keep your lips moisturised for a few days before, and avoid lip scrubs and peeling products.
  • Tell us about recent lip fillers, medicines and any reactions to tattoos or pigments.
  • Come without lipstick, and bring photos of lip colours you like.

Aftercare in the first weeks

Lips heal quickly but need gentle care. For the first week, keep them clean and moisturised with the balm the clinic recommends, avoid lipstick and lip scrubs, and keep them out of direct sun. Very hot, salty or spicy food can sting, so milder meals are easier for a few days. Flaking usually starts around the third day; picking the flakes can pull out pigment and leave patches. After healing, a lip balm with sunscreen helps the colour last longer.

Risks and how they are reduced

Most people heal without problems, but lip PMU is a cosmetic tattoo and has some risks. Cold sores can be triggered in people who carry the herpes simplex virus, which is why antiviral cover may be advised. Infection is reduced with sterile technique and single-use needles. Allergic reactions to pigment are possible, and a review of lip tattoo complications notes that red pigments are most often linked to reactions and that patch tests cannot predict every reaction. Rarely, lumps can form in the lips months later; any lump, persistent swelling or change in the lips should be checked by a doctor. Uneven or unwanted colour can often be improved with a PMU correction plan.

What affects the cost of lip blush?

The cost depends on whether you choose a tint, a lip line, neutralization or a combination, whether you are having a first treatment or a refresh, and whether the touch-up is included. Dark lips needing neutralization may need more sessions. Your artist explains the plan and total at your consultation.

FAQs

Frequently Asked Questions

How long does lip blush last?
Lip blush usually lasts two to three years before it needs a refresh. It fades faster with sun exposure, smoking, and exfoliating lip products. A colour refresh on healed lips is usually quicker than the first treatment.
Does lip blush hurt?
A numbing cream is used, so most people feel a light scratching or vibration rather than pain. Lips are more sensitive than brows, and they are usually swollen and tender for a day or two afterwards.
Can lip blush lighten dark lips?
Lip neutralization can make dark lips look lighter and more even by layering warm pigment first. It often needs more than one session, and the result depends on your starting colour. It does not change the cause, so sun protection and not smoking help the result last.
What if I get cold sores?
Tell us before booking. Lip tattooing can trigger a cold sore in people who carry the virus. A guideline in the Journal of Clinical and Aesthetic Dermatology describes antiviral tablets started before a procedure for people at risk, so a doctor may prescribe them. We will not treat lips with an active cold sore.
Why does my lip colour look patchy after a week?
This is a normal part of healing. As the lips flake, the colour can look faded or uneven, and it gradually comes back over the next few weeks. Any gaps that remain are filled at the touch-up session.
How do I look after my lips while they heal?
Keep your lips clean, apply the balm the clinic recommends, and avoid lipstick, very hot or spicy food, and direct sun for the first week. Drink through a straw if it is more comfortable, and let flakes come off on their own.
